To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the kidneys of the animals were the organs that accumulated the highest radioactivity, after the i.p. administration of 125 I-labelled Fab antidigital antibodies.
Fab antidigoxin antibodies are rapidly cleared from the circulation, mainly by the kidneys, where they are accumulated.
125I-labelled F(ab')2 and Fab antidigitalis antibody fragments are rapidly eliminated from the circulation, mainly by the kidney.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an experimental model for the study of digitalis-like factors in the rat kidney.
the development of radioiodinated Fab antibodies against the digitalis-like factor, which may be useful in the diagnosis of digitalis intoxication.

the question of the possible accumulation of digitalis-like factors in the kidneys after the administration, of 125I-Fab antidigitalis antibodies, and with the possible role of endogenous digitalis like factors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the radioiodinated antibodies were not accumulated in the rat kidneys, as was previously thought, but that they were rapidly excreted by the kidneys.

125I-labelled Fabs of antidigitalis antibodies accumulate preferentially in kidneys of rats, and the radioactivity in the kidneys is not only due to the radioiodine, which is released from the antibody.
the accumulation of radioactivity is due to both the presence of the endogenous digoxin-like substance and the uptake of released radioiodine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Fab fragments are not suitable for radioimmunological studies of digitalis-like factors, because of the preferential accumulation of radioiodine in the kidneys.
125I-labelled Fabs accumulate in the kidneys, but that the radioactivity does not result from the uptake of the endogenous digoxin.

the kidneys are a site of preferential uptake of 125I-Fab antidigitalis antibodies and the radioactivity in the kidney homogenate may be due to both the antibodies and the endogenous digital-like factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the kidneys are an important organ to study for endogenous digitalis like factors.
it is possible to produce antibodies that can selectively target digitalis-like factors.
we can now make the case that the kidneys are a potential source of digitalis-like factor (DLF), and that this factor is produced in the kidney.
